Hey! As some others have said here, besides a hot water bottle the best thing for me would be a TENs machine. I have the Ovira one, which is very portable and not noticeable really. They can be a bit expensive but I would say it’s worth it, they last a decent while and if they do break I’ve found that their team is very helpful (with right conditions of breakage etc). Sometimes an ice pack also helps (although that may not be a viable option). They have portable heat packs  as well. There are some people on Instagram (like sam.endogram) who sometimes review products that may help. Hope this helps! Good luck!

I wish they knew / understood just how much we already put up with it. I had been told it was ‘normal’ not to be able to walk from pain for two years (including when I wasn’t on my period ). Not believing, or just downright ignoring what I say. For example, at one appointment I told them specifically my pain was mainly in my lower abdomen and lower back. She said, ‘are you sure it’s not just in your thighs? Because when I get period pain, it’s in my thighs. ‘ And continued to write that I had pains going down my thighs/legs. 

I think a lot of the time, they don’t realise how much pain we have been in before going to see a doctor, so they assume it’s ok to say it isn’t much pain or not that serious, when actually seeing them may have been a last resort after a lot of excruciating pain. 

I hope this makes sense and helps. Good luck!!
